subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. If those are 50 deg and 60 deg, what is the exterior angle?
questions.explain: Exterior angle = 50 + 60 = 110 deg.

questions.q: Two angles in a triangle are 55° and 65°. What is the third angle?
questions.explain: Angles in a triangle sum to 180°, so 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°.

questions.q: Two angles lie on a straight line. One is 110°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°, so 180° − 110° = 70°.

questions.q: A circle has diameter 10 cm. What is its area? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
questions.explain: Radius = 5 cm, so area = π × 5^2 = π × 25 ≈ 78.5 cm^2.

questions.q: What is the exact value of cos 30°?
questions.explain: cos 30° = √3/2 is a standard exact value.

questions.q: What is the value of tan 45°?
questions.explain: tan 45° = 1 since opposite equals adjacent.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explain: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs 9 cm and 12 cm. What is the hypotenuse?
To find a missing side when you know an angle and the hypotenuse and need the adjacent, which ratio is used?
questions.explain: Adjacent and hypotenuse are linked by cos.

questions.q: A line drawn from the centre of a circle to a point on the circumference is called the:
questions.explain: A radius joins the centre to the circumference.

questions.q: In a right-angled triangle, which ratio equals the opposite divided by the hypotenuse?
questions.explain: By SOHCAHTOA, sin = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 40°. What is each base angle?
questions.explain: The two equal base angles share 180° − 40° = 140°, so each is 70°.

questions.q: A cuboid measures 4 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explain: Volume = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 cm^3.

questions.q: A triangular prism has a triangular cross-section of area 15 cm^2 and length 9 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explain: Volume = cross-sectional area x length = 15 x 9 = 135 cm^3.

questions.q: Four angles meet at a point. Three are 85 deg, 95 deg and 100 deg. What is the fourth?
questions.explain: Angles around a point sum to 360 deg, so 360 - 85 - 95 - 100 = 80 deg.

questions.q: What is the exact value of sin 45°?
questions.explain: sin 45° = √2/2 (equivalently 1/√2) is a standard exact value.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 10 and an angle of 30°. The opposite side equals 10 × sin 30°. What is its length?
A trapezium has parallel sides 7 cm and 11 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?
An L-shape is made from a 10 cm by 8 cm rectangle with a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle removed. What is its area?
Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 100° and 80°. What is the fourth angle?
questions.explain: Angles in a quadrilateral sum to 360°, so 360° − 90° − 100° − 80° = 90°.
